source.check: returned unopposed: named in the Impartial Reporter's nominations report of 21 May 1964 (p. 7) among 'the other nominations, which remain unchanged'; the county council was uncontested

note: Triennial election, polled Thursday 4 June 1964 (Notice of Election, Fermanagh Herald, 2 May 1964, p. 8). The county council was uncontested; the only contest in the county was the Colebrooke seat on Lisnaskea Rural Council (Irish News, 28 May 1964; Belfast Telegraph, 30 May 1964, p. 7). The Telegraph of 30 May 1964 lists the changes in the county council selection: Mr. Albert James Vaughan takes the place of Mr. George A. Cathcart for the Laragh division (printed 'Lurgh'), Mr. David Brien replaces Mr. Thomas C. Hurst at Ballinamallard, Mr. Albert Anderson replaces Mr. William Phillips at Clonelly, Mr. Irvine Johnston replaces Mr. John J. McElroy at Irvinestown, and Mr. John Ferguson replaces Mr. James Saunderson at Monea. The remaining fifteen members are named in the Impartial Reporter of 21 May 1964, p. 7, as 'the other nominations, which remain unchanged' (added 6 Nov 2026, replacing members previously carried from the 1961 return). One qualification: Cathcart had taken Laragh after the 1961 election, so the change there is measured against the outgoing council rather than against the 1961 result; the 1964 member, Vaughan, is unaffected. Returned unopposed.
